items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: I didn't know King Oliver, I didn't know Buddy Bowling.

ctx.x: Well I didn't hear many variations there. He sounded like he was playing pretty much the melody.

Well yeah well I mean you if you're talking about get off or something like that. Maybe that what you mean. Yeah did Perez get off? Little not much. I wouldn't say a whole lot. See them fellas sometimes he didn't do like like Buddy Petit and Renny and then when we come up. See them fellas they play straight stuff. Mmhmm. And they started putting extra stuff in this stuff here. Later and Buddy and Renny and them time from what I can see. King Oliver and them kind of fellas. They started putting you know more to…
It was big and little Kato. Two piano players. Dad used to talk to us about that. What about Bonk? How did he play in the olden days? When you first heard?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: King Oliver was gone. Johnny Dots was gone. I met them in Chicago.

ctx.x: Where did you hear Blind Willie Dunn?

I heard his records. Oh, yeah. Well, you know, Lonnie Johnson played guitar with Blind Willie Dunn, and some of them are reported to have... They have two guitars. Yeah. It's been reported that King Oliver played on one of the records. To me, it didn't sound like it. How about you? Did it sound like it to you?
Well, that's what Johnny Wiggs says, and he heard Oliver in person. He said he was just playing his old style that he played before he went to normal.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: I don't know. I've never heard him do that.

ctx.x: How many trumpet players would have that style?
Oh, boy, a lot when I first came here. Joe Oliver, Kimball. Well, to the truth, everybody, that fella Clem used to play like that, too. He changed a little bit. He used to play like that.
That's with that heavy tongue in, huh, Kyle? Hmm? Your tongue a lot to get that.
